scope: Proposition 4.11 (Cases for a prepared interval) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Use the notation of Proposition 4.9, in the core quotient. Let Λ ≤ Aut(S) be the image of a coordinate stabilizer in H, and put I = Λ ∩ S, identifying S with its inner automorphisms. The following are the only possibilities. (i) c(P) = Ss. All labels are subdirect. If the interval represents the whole L, its opposite has an ordinary subgroup representation with top-group order at most |H| < |G|. (ii) P = c(P) ̸= 1. The interval is isomorphic to the ordinary almost simple interval [Λ, SΛ]. (iii) P = 1 and I = S. Every nonbottom label is subdirect, and the dual interval is the extension poset of Lemma 4.10 with one artificial top adjoined. In particular the cases P < c(P) < Ss, P = 1 with I = 1, and P = 1 with 1 < I < S are impossible.
